To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the B. subtilsis primosome is assembled on DNA substrates that resemble a reactivated replication fork, in a sequential order that involves the binding of PriA to single-stranded DNA, followed by the binding of DnaD and DnaB.
the DnaD and DnaB proteins of B. subti lis are involved in primosomal assembly, and their binding to DNA is stimulated by PriA.
“The B. subtilispriA, dnaD, dnaB, dnaI genes encode the primosomal proteins that assemble on forked DNA in a sequential PriA, Dnal, DnaD/Dnal, Dnal/DnaD/Dnal order.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early steps of primosome assembly.
the early steps of primosome assembly in B. subtilsis.
the identification of primosomal proteins in B. subtilus, and the characterization of the interactions between these proteins and their partners in the context of primosome assembly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the B. subtilsis primosome is composed of at least three subassemblies: PriA-DnaB, DdaB-DnaD and DnaB-DnaD.
primosome assembly is sequential in E. coli and in B. subtilsis.
the primosome assembly is sequential in B. subtilispriA, dnaD, dnaB order and is initiated on a DNA substrate mimicking a stalled fork.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DnaB, and DnaD and DnaI proteins ofB. subtilis, which are involved in primosomal functions both at the origin and at arrested forks, are all multimeric and interact with each other and with the PriA protein on DNA.
DnaD and DnaB are the two major primosomal proteins of B. subtlis.
DnaB and, more particularly, DnaD are essential for the assembly of a primosome inB. subtilis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B. subtilisis primosome has an extended role compared to the E. coli primosome.
B. subtilsis primosome assembly is similar to that in E. coli, but with a distinct set of primosomal proteins.
the primosome assembly in B. subtilies is different from the one observed in E. coli and that it is not restricted to the reactivation of stalled DNA replication forks.
